sources.fact: From 16 April 2026 the new Appeal a planning decision service became the primary route for most new planning/enforcement appeals; legacy ACP remains for existing/unsupported cases.
Planning appeals can concern refusal, objectionable conditions or non-determination; the appellant must provide planning application number and decision date.
Finding an appeal uses the 7 digit appeal/case reference or postcode, and users may need to search both ACP and the new service during transition.
GOV.UK provides routes to appeal or search planning decisions/notices across multiple appeal types.
Planning Inspectorate publishes detailed data on a selection of casework decisions over a rolling 5 year period; last updated 25 June 2026.
Casework data can contain blanks and can change between publications; older data removes identifying case/address fields under retention policy.
Enforcement, listed-building enforcement and lawful-development-certificate appeals moved into the new service during early 2026 rollout.
An enforcement appeal must identify the LPA/site/effective date and be received before the enforcement notice effective date.
A separate procedural guide applies to appeals relating to applications submitted on or after 1 April 2026.
All English LPAs were onboarded to the new online appeals service by 1 December 2025 while legacy cases stayed on ACP.
Legacy ACP still supports case lookup by the final 7 digits of an appeal reference for relevant retained cases.
Published casework data covers decided cases in the rolling window and excludes in-progress, withdrawn or turned-away appeals.

examples.result: Exact Planning Inspectorate case reference is required before binding an appeal to a candidate planning application.
Postcode search is discovery-only and does not substitute for exact case/application/site matching.
An appeal being lodged does not imply allowed, dismissed or withdrawn outcome.
Casework database absence is not evidence of no appeal because in-progress/withdrawn/turned-away and retention gaps exist.
ACP/new-service split is treated as a transition routing issue, not duplicate appeal evidence.
Allowed/dismissed statistics are not converted into parcel-level appeal probability.
Appeal decision is kept distinct from the underlying LPA permission and later condition/discharge history.
No appeal-based promotion occurs without exact case reference, application reference, site and current outcome evidence.
